2608.30856.title: You Shouldn't Have Asked: A Pragmatics-Inspired Taxonomy for Evaluating LLM Refusals
2608.30856.paper_summary: Refusals are often treated as face-threatening acts in pragmatics because they can challenge the requester's socially claimed self-image. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained to refuse unsafe and inappropriate requests, and these refusals may harm users when models fail to manage this interactional cost properly. While existing work has mainly approached LLM non-compliance as a safety-alignment outcome, it does not provide a way to evaluate whether LLMs refuse appropriately across different harmful contexts. To study this question, we propose (to our knowledge) the first taxonomy of LLM refusals that is grounded in pragmatic theory. Applying this taxonomy to responses from 16 modern LLMs across 14 harm categories, we find that although models differ in how they refuse, their refusals are overall explicit and strongly morally evaluative, with interactional repair occurring mainly through offering or providing safer alternatives instead of interpersonal facework. This pattern is especially consequential in sensitive harm contexts, where overuse of negative framing may make users feel shamed or provoked, undermining the purpose of safe non-compliance. We therefore call for alignment evaluation that considers not only whether models refuse harmful requests, but also whether they refuse in ways that are contextually adaptive and socially accountable for the interactional consequences of saying no.
2608.30856.paper_summary_zh: 拒絕在語用學中常被視為威脅面子的行為，因為它們可能挑戰請求者所聲稱的社會自我形象。大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被訓練以拒絕不安全和不當的請求，而當模型未能妥善管理這種互動成本時，這些拒絕可能會對用戶造成傷害。雖然現有的研究主要將LLM的不合規視為安全對齊的結果，但並未提供評估LLMs在不同有害情境中是否適當拒絕的方式。為了研究這個問題，我們提出（據我們所知）第一個基於語用理論的LLM拒絕分類法。將這一分類法應用於來自16個現代LLMs在14個危害類別中的回應，我們發現儘管模型在拒絕的方式上有所不同，但它們的拒絕整體上是明確且強烈道德評價的，互動修復主要是通過提供或提供更安全的替代方案，而不是人際面子工作。在敏感的危害情境中，這一模式尤其具有重要意義，因為過度使用負面框架可能會讓用戶感到羞愧或被激怒，從而削弱安全不合規的目的。因此，我們呼籲進行對齊評估，不僅考慮模型是否拒絕有害請求，還要考慮它們是否以上下文適應和社會負責的方式拒絕，對說不的互動後果負責。
